Here are a few options, ranging from slightly rephrased to more formal, depending on your context:

**Option 1 (Slightly more concise and direct):**

> "As suggested, going forward, please **always include the `sql_id`** in your requests to the L2/L4 team for query tuning. This will help prevent unnecessary back-and-forth and expedite the investigation."

**Option 2 (Emphasizing the benefit):**

> "To avoid delays and streamline the investigation, please ensure you **explicitly include the `sql_id`** in all future query tuning requests sent to the L2/L4 team, as we discussed."

**Option 3 (More formal/instructional):**

> "In line with our recent discussion, all future query tuning requests submitted to the L2/L4 team **must explicitly specify the `sql_id`**. This standardization will eliminate follow-up inquiries and accelerate the diagnostic process."

**Option 4 (Short and to the point):**

> "As discussed, from now on, please **include the `sql_id` in all query tuning requests** to L2/L4. This will prevent delays."

**Key improvements made:**

*   **"specifically mention the sql_id"** changed to more natural phrasing like "always include the `sql_id`," "explicitly include the `sql_id`," or "must explicitly specify the `sql_id`."
*   **"so there is no back and forth questioning delaying the investigation"** rephrased to be more concise and positive, focusing on the desired outcome: "prevent unnecessary back-and-forth and expedite the investigation," "avoid delays and streamline the investigation," "eliminate follow-up inquiries and accelerate the diagnostic process," or "prevent delays."
*   Added stronger verbs like "ensure," "must," "always," or "explicitly" to reinforce the instruction.

Choose the option that best fits the tone and formality of your communication.
